meta.financial_picture: 1) Pre-deal scale: CET's April 2020 PPP loan ($2.062M, 121 jobs) implies about $9.9M of annual payroll. At the 30–40% labor-to-revenue ratio typical of commercial electrical contractors, 2019 revenue was roughly $25–33M. 2) By October 2025 CET reported about 140 employees (the brief's ~160 'licensed professionals' may count differently). Applying $250–375k revenue per employee, bracketed by IES Holdings' ~$328k, gives 2025 standalone revenue of about $35–55M (midpoint ~$45M). 3) At the 8–12% EBITDA margins seen at Limbach (~10%) and IES (~13%, high end), CET's standalone EBITDA at entry was probably about $3–6M, a true lower-middle-market platform. 4) The equity structure supports that scale. The only co-invest was one LP writing $7.5M (Form D, first sale 2025-02-05), from a ~$335M fund where a typical position is $25–50M. Total equity was therefore likely ~$25–45M. 5) Applying the brief's 3.5–5.5x LMM leverage to $3–6M of EBITDA implies $10–33M of senior debt at close. Entry enterprise value was likely ~$35–75M (~9–12x), but none of the debt is visible. 6) No BDC schedule, lender press release, Form D debt vehicle or credit rating names CET, 'CET Acquisition Holdings, LLC' or Horton. EDGAR full-text search found zero hits and 73 downloaded BDC/credit-fund filings were negative. So the facility most likely sits with a bank or a non-SEC-reporting private lender or SBIC. 7) Broad Sky's March 2026 Form ADV marks the CET co-invest vehicle at $8.504M against $7.5M invested (1.13x gross). That modest markup fits the NuWave tuck-in plus organic growth, not a re-rating. 8) NuWave was tiny at acquisition (PPP: 4 jobs in 2020, founded 2019) and adds engineering/design-build capability, not scale; call it $2–10M of revenue (low confidence). 9) Horton is the transformational add-on. Its 2020 PPP ($646k, 42 jobs, ~$3.1M payroll) has grown to 120+ staff, so revenue is plausibly ~$25–40M today. CET says the deal 'nearly doubles' the workforce. 10) Pro forma for both add-ons, the platform is roughly 260–290 employees, $65–100M revenue and $6–11M EBITDA (low confidence). Horton was bought by the CET LLC subsidiary with no new Broad Sky Form D, so it was likely funded with incremental or delayed-draw debt plus seller rollover, pushing leverage toward the upper half of the 3.5–5.5x band. 11) Offsetting positives: a clean OSHA history, no material litigation, full PPP forgiveness, and state-funded program work (MassCEC On-Street Charging prime vendor, CT Clean Water Fund wastewater exposure via Horton). Watch items: a likely related-party lease of Horton's Canton facility (97 River Road CBP, LLC) and a possible Duquette-affiliated mechanical firm (A. Duquette & Son) across the street from CET HQ.

key_figures.entity_type: Delaware LLC, pooled private equity fund, not 40-Act registered

items.what_it_tells_us: This is the only SEC filing tied directly to the CET deal. It dates the closing to about February 5, 2025, about six weeks before the March 19 announcement. A single $7.5M co-investor sat alongside Broad Sky Partners, LP, so the fund wrote most of the equity check. The co-invest is small next to Broad Sky's Thomas Scientific co-invests (about $35.9M and $59.6M), which points to a much smaller deal.

It suggests CET was held above cost, but gross asset value can include cash or fee accruals, so it is not a clean read on equity value.
